mainTopic: Sifting flour again on יום טוב, asking regular sellers for food on יום טוב, and the start of a new chapter on carrying in an unusual way
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: שמואל spoke to teach the practical הלכה. A ברייתא then records a מחלוקת about sifting flour a second time on יום טוב. Everyone agrees that sifting is allowed if a pebble or wood chip fell in. רבינא rejects a version that allows picking the pebble out by hand, because that looks like בורר. רבא בר רב הונא זוטי publicly permits a second sifting, and רב נחמן replies that the teaching was unnecessary, since everyone in נהרדעא already did it. Two stories follow about the wives of רב יוסף and רב אשי sifting in unusual ways. A new משנה and ברייתא then allow asking a regular seller on יום טוב for items by number or for single items, as long as no measure or price is mentioned. The chapter אין צדין ends, and a new chapter opens with how to carry wine jugs and straw on יום טוב. That ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל was teaching the practical הלכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion. It explains that שמואל's statement was meant to teach the הלכה למעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל came to teach us the practical הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier question about why שמואל needed to say his ruling. Its answer is that he came to tell us the practical הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was an earlier source that allowed the practice. Someone might ask what שמואל adds by speaking. The answer is that he was telling us how to actually act, even though a ברייתא says something different.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical ruling; how to actually act

phrases.english: Shmuel — the practical halacha
he came to teach us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from before this section about the purpose of שמואל's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the purpose of the statement: it gives the practical ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's statement teaches what to do in practice, even though a ברייתא says otherwise.

steps.title: A ברייתא's dispute about sifting flour again on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת about sifting flour a second time on יום טוב. Both sides agree it is allowed if a pebble or wood chip fell in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: one may not sift flour a second time on יום טוב. In the name of רבי פפייס and רבי יהודה בן בתירא they said: one may sift it again. All agree that if a pebble or wood chip fell into it, one may sift it again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. In it, the תנא קמא forbids sifting flour a second time on יום טוב, and רבי פפייס and רבי יהודה בן בתירא permit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flour was already sifted before יום טוב. A second sifting only makes it a bit finer, so the first opinion sees it as needless extra effort. Everyone agrees that if a pebble or chip fell in, sifting is allowed, because now there is a real need.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means sifting a second time, not learning

steps.confusionAlert: שׁוֹנִין here has nothing to do with learning or reviewing. It comes from doing something a second time, meaning sifting the flour again.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not sift flour a second time on Yom Tov.
In the name of Rabbi Papeyyas
and Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira they said:
One may sift it again.
And they agree that if there fell into it
phrases.notes: A pebble fell into the flour after it had already been sifted once.

phrases.english: a pebble or a wood chip, that one may sift it again.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין שׁוֹנִין קֶמַח בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the ברייתא about a second sifting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת about sifting flour a second time on יום טוב. Everyone agrees it is permitted if a pebble or chip fell in.

steps.title: A different version of the ברייתא before רבינא
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a version that forbids sifting again. In his version, if a pebble or chip fell in, one picks it out by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רבינא: one may not sift flour a second time on יום טוב, but if a pebble or wood chip fell in, he picks it out by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: A reciter of ברייתות says his version of the teaching in front of רבינא. In this version, the fix for a fallen pebble is picking it out by hand, not sifting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version agrees that sifting again is forbidden. It changes the pebble case: instead of sifting, it allows removing the pebble by hand. This sets up רבינא's reaction in the next step.

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Ravina:
phrases.notes: Here תנא means a person whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות, not one of the Sages of the משנה.

phrases.english: One may not sift flour a second time on Yom Tov,
but if a pebble or a wood chip fell in —
he picks it out with his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of the same ברייתא, with a different ruling for the pebble case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sifting again is forbidden, but a fallen pebble or chip may be picked out by hand.

steps.title: רבינא: picking by hand is even worse
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rejects the תנא's version. Picking out the pebble by hand is even more forbidden, because it looks like בורר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: all the more so it is forbidden, because it is like selecting.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא tells the תנא that his version cannot be right. Picking out a pebble by hand is even more forbidden than sifting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking the bad piece out of the food with your hand looks like the מלאכה of בורר. If sifting again is a problem, picking by hand is certainly a problem. So the correct teaching is the first ברייתא: in the pebble case one sifts the flour.

keyTerms.meaning: Selecting; one of the forbidden מלאכות

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a pebble in the flour should be removed by sifting, not by picking it out by hand.

phrases.english: He said to him:
All the more so it is forbidden,
since it is like selecting.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּאָסוּר, דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ כְּבוֹרֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the version recited in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא's version that allows picking out the pebble by hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Picking by hand looks like בורר. That makes it worse than sifting, so it cannot be the allowed method.

steps.title: רבא בר רב הונא זוטי teaches publicly that a second sifting is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב הונא זוטי publicly teaches at the entrance of נהרדעא that one may sift flour again on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב הונא זוטי expounded at the entrance of נהרדעא: one may sift flour a second time on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: A Sage gives a public teaching ruling like the lenient opinion. He says sifting flour again on יום טוב is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He follows רבי פפייס and רבי יהודה בן בתירא from the ברייתא. This sets up רב נחמן's reaction in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא זוּטֵי
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Huna the Short expounded
at the entrance of Neharde'a:
One may sift flour a second time on Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא זוּטֵי אַפִּתְחָא דִנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a public ruling that follows the lenient opinion in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may sift flour a second time on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב נחמן: the teaching was not needed, everyone already sifts
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן sends word that this teaching was unnecessary. Many sieves were already in use in נהרדעא, so people were already doing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to them: go out and tell אבא, your good deed has been thrown on thorns. Go out and see how many sieves go around in נהרדעא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן reacts to the public teaching. He says it adds nothing, because everyone in נהרדעא was already sifting flour again on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן does not argue with the ruling. He is pushing aside the need to teach it, since the practice was already common. In effect, his remark shows the lenient practice was widely accepted.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the ruling is wrong. He is saying it was not needed, because people were already doing it.
steps.whatToRemember: Sifting flour a second time on יום טוב is a מחלוקת in the ברייתא. If a pebble fell in, everyone allows sifting, but picking it out by hand is worse because it looks like בורר. The lenient practice was so common in נהרדעא that teaching it was unnecessary.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to them:
Go out and say to Abba:
phrases.notes: אבא is רבא בר רב הונא; the name רבא is short for רב אבא.

phrases.english: Your good is taken
and thrown on the thorns,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected wording. He means your teaching is going to waste.

phrases.english: Go out and see
how many sieves go around in Neharde'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוּקוּ וֶאֱמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְאַבָּא: שְׁקִילָא טֵיבוּתָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 5 by pushing aside the need for the public teaching.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the need to teach it publicly, not the lenient ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The teaching adds nothing, because the practice was already widespread in נהרדעא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Sifting again on יום טוב was already common practice in נהרדעא.

steps.title: רב יוסף's wife sifts on the back of the sieve
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's wife sifted flour on the back of a sieve on יום טוב. He hinted that she could sift normally because he wanted good bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף's wife was sifting flour on the back of the sieve. He said to her: Look, I want good bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about sifting on יום טוב. רב יוסף's wife sifted in an unusual, changed way, and he hinted that she did not need to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turning the sieve over is a שינוי, a change from the normal weekday way. Sifting on the back does a poorer job. רב יוסף wanted good bread, so he was hinting that normal sifting is fine, in line with the lenient teaching in Step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: doing something in a changed, unusual way

phrases.english: The wife of Rav Yosef
was sifting flour on the back of the sieve.
phrases.notes: She turned the sieve upside down so the sifting would be different from a regular weekday.

phrases.english: He said to her:
Look, I want good-quality bread.
phrases.notes: He is hinting that she can sift the regular way.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף נָהֲלָא קִמְחָא אַגַּבָּא דְּמַהוֹלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical story that continues the topic of sifting again on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A change in how one sifts is not required. רב יוסף preferred normal sifting for good bread.

steps.title: רב אשי learns from his wife's careful family practice
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי's wife sifted flour onto a table instead of into a bowl. רב אשי said she must have seen this in the home of her father, רמי בר חמא, who was very careful in his practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי's wife was sifting flour onto a table. רב אשי said: This wife of ours is the daughter of רמי בר חמא, and רמי בר חמא was a man of careful practice. If she had not seen it in her father's house, she would not have done it.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story shows a wife sifting in a changed way, onto a table. רב אשי says her practice can be trusted because she learned it in her careful father's home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sifting onto a table instead of into the usual bowl is another kind of שינוי. רב אשי does not question it. He treats it as a real practice handed down from רמי בר חמא, so it supports the idea that sifting with a change is a proper way to do it on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: a master of deeds; someone very careful in practice
from her family's home (her father's house)

phrases.english: The wife of Rav Ashi
was sifting flour onto a table.
Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דִּידַן, בְּרַתֵּיה דְּרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא,
phrases.english: This one of ours is the daughter of Rami bar Chama,
phrases.notes: "This one of ours" is his way of saying "my wife."

phrases.aramaic: וְרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מָרָא דְעוֹבָדָא הֲוָה,
phrases.english: and Rami bar Chama was a master of good deeds,
and if she had not seen it in her father's house,
she would not have done it.

steps.whatToRemember: Both stories involve sifting with a change: on the back of the sieve, or onto a table. רב אשי treats a practice learned in a careful home as a reliable model.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָאו דַּחֲזַאי מִבֵּי נָשָׁא לָא הֲוָה עָבְדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story about sifting with a change. This time the practice is used as a model to follow.
steps.raayaObject: Sifting on יום טוב with a change (onto a table) is a proper practice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רמי בר חמא's household, which his daughter brought with her.

steps.title: משנה: asking your regular grocer for items by number
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that on יום טוב a person may go to his regular grocer and ask for eggs and nuts by number, because people count this way at home too.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may go to a grocer he usually buys from and say to him: Give me eggs and nuts by number, since a homeowner normally counts like this in his own house.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The משנה allows a person on יום טוב to ask his regular grocer for a certain number of eggs and nuts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Buying and selling is not allowed on יום טוב. Saying a number of eggs is allowed because people count this way at home, so it does not sound like a business deal. Going to someone you usually use means you can settle the bill later without awkwardness.

keyTerms.meaning: a homeowner; the head of a household

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A person may go to a grocer
whom he usually buys from, and say to him:
Give me eggs and nuts by number,
since it is the way of a homeowner
to count inside his own house.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for getting food from stores on יום טוב: speak in a homey way, not a business way.
steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹלֵךְ אָדָם אֵצֶל חֶנְוָנִי הָרָגִיל אֶצְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may ask a regular grocer for eggs and nuts by number on יום טוב, because counting is normal at home.

steps.title: ברייתא: asking a shepherd, butcher, poultry seller or baker for one item
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא extends the משנה. You may ask a regular shepherd, butcher, poultry seller or baker for a single item.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person may go to a shepherd he usually deals with and say, give me one kid or one lamb; to his butcher, give me one foreleg or one thigh; to his poultry seller, give me one turtledove or one young pigeon; to his baker, give me one loaf or one fine roll.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that applies the משנה's rule to other kinds of sellers. In each case the person asks for one item from someone he usually deals with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each example uses the same pattern: a regular seller, and asking for one specific item. Naming a single animal, cut of meat or loaf sounds like a household request, not a business deal.

keyTerms.meaning: someone who fattens and sells birds

phrases.english: Gemara: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹלֵךְ אָדָם אֵצֶל רוֹעֶה הָרָגִיל אֶצְלוֹ
phrases.english: A person may go to a shepherd he usually deals with

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר לוֹ: תֵּן לִי גְּדִי אֶחָד אוֹ טָלֶה אֶחָד.
phrases.english: and say to him: Give me one kid or one lamb.
To a butcher he usually buys from,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר לוֹ: תֵּן לִי כַּף אַחַת אוֹ יָרֵךְ אַחַת.
phrases.english: and say to him: Give me one foreleg or one thigh.
To a poultry seller he usually buys from,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר לוֹ: תֵּן לִי תּוֹר אֶחָד אוֹ גּוֹזָל אֶחָד.
phrases.english: and say to him: Give me one turtledove or one young pigeon.
To a baker he usually buys from,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר לוֹ: תֵּן לִי כִּכָּר אֶחָד אוֹ גְּלוּסְקָא אַחַת.
phrases.english: and say to him: Give me one loaf or one fine roll.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן הוֹלֵךְ אָדָם אֵצֶל רוֹעֶה הָרָגִיל אֶצְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's grocer case to other kinds of sellers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Asking a regular seller for one item on יום טוב is allowed.

steps.title: ברייתא: the grocer case, numbers yes but no measure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא repeats the grocer case with examples of numbers. It adds the condition that one may not mention a measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And to a grocer he usually buys from, he may say: Give me twenty eggs, or fifty nuts, ten peaches, five pomegranates, and one אתרוג, as long as he does not mention a measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא turns to the grocer and gives examples of asking by number. Then it sets a limit: do not name a unit of measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting items sounds like home use, but naming a measure such as a קב sounds like a store sale. So the ברייתא allows numbers and forbids measures.

keyTerms.meaning: as long as; on condition that
an amount by measure (such as a קַב or a סְאָה)

phrases.english: And to a grocer he usually buys from,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר לוֹ: תֵּן לִי עֶשְׂרִים בֵּיצִים,
phrases.english: and say to him: Give me twenty eggs,
or fifty nuts, ten peaches,
and five pomegranates and one etrog.

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַזְכִּיר לוֹ סְכוּם מִדָּה.
phrases.english: As long as he does not mention to him a measure.
phrases.notes: He means a unit like a קב. Saying "a קב of nuts" sounds like a store sale, but counting does not.

steps.confusionAlert: Numbers are allowed, but measures are not. "Twenty eggs" is fine. Naming a unit of volume or weight is not.
steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַזְכִּיר לוֹ סְכוּם מִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the grocer case and adds a limiting condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may ask a grocer for items by number, but not by measure.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: do not mention the price
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives a different condition: one may not mention the price of the purchase.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: As long as he does not mention to him the price of the purchase.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא gives a different limit. For רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, the problem is mentioning money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion worried about naming a measure. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר worries about naming a price. Talking about money on יום טוב makes it a business deal, so the bill should be worked out after יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: the amount of the purchase (its price)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַזְכִּיר לוֹ סְכוּם מִקָּח.
phrases.english: As long as he does not mention to him the price of the purchase.

steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב you may ask a regular seller for items by number or for single items. The first opinion forbids mentioning a measure, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר forbids mentioning a price.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַזְכִּיר לוֹ סְכוּם מִקָּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different condition from the first opinion in Step 11: price instead of measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not mention the price of the purchase on יום טוב.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter אין צדין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally finishes the third chapter of ביצה, called אין צדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter אין צדין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the traditional goodbye to the chapter we just finished. It is not part of the argument. It marks that the chapter אין צדין is complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every chapter of the גמרא ends with הדרן עלך plus the chapter's name. The chapter is named after its opening words, אין צדין, 'one may not trap'. The discussion about buying from a grocer on יום טוב ends here.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the formula said when a chapter is finished.
One may not trap. These are the opening words and the name of the third chapter of ביצה.

steps.whatToRemember: The chapter אין צדין is finished. Everything that follows belongs to a new chapter with a new topic.

phrases.english: We will return to you, [chapter] 'One may not trap'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the ברייתא and the view of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר about buying from a grocer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The third chapter of ביצה, אין צדין, is complete.

steps.title: New chapter: carrying wine jugs on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that on יום טוב one may not carry wine jugs in a basket or tub. He may carry them on his shoulder or in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who moves jugs of wine from one place to another on יום טוב should not carry them in a basket or a tub. He may carry them on his shoulder or in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a new משנה. It says that carrying wine jugs on יום טוב is allowed, but only in a certain way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not forbid moving the wine. It only limits how it is moved. A basket or tub is the normal weekday way to haul many jugs, so the משנה requires carrying them on the shoulder or in front of the body instead.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying that carrying is forbidden on יום טוב. Carrying is allowed here. The משנה only controls the manner of carrying.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the theme of the new chapter: even permitted work on יום טוב should be done differently from the normal weekday way.

phrases.english: One who brings jugs of wine
from place to place
may not bring them in a basket or in a tub
but he may bring [them]
on his shoulder or in front of him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב, wine jugs may be carried on the shoulder or in front of a person, but not in a basket or tub.

steps.title: Carrying straw on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה applies the same idea to straw. One may not sling the basket over his back, but he may carry it in his hand. Then it starts its next ruling with ומתחילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the same way, someone carrying straw should not sling the basket onto his back. He may carry it in his hand. And one may begin...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second example of the same rule, this time with straw. Its final word starts the next ruling of the משנה, which continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וכן, 'and similarly', tells us this follows the same idea as the wine jugs. Slinging a basket behind the back is the normal way to carry a load, so on יום טוב it is carried in the hand instead. The word ומתחילין opens a new ruling that we have not reached yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Sling or hoist onto the back
And one may begin. This opens the next ruling of the משנה.

phrases.english: And similarly, one who carries the straw
may not sling the basket behind him
but he may bring it in his hand
And one may begin

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses וכן ('similarly') to apply the same principle from the wine jugs case to carrying straw.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב, straw may be carried in a basket held in the hand, but the basket may not be slung onto one's back.
